cards.explanation: The answer is True. David calls himself "…the one anointed by the God of Jacob…" (2 Samuel 23:1). Notice he doesn't say he made himself king. He says God anointed him. Titles are way easier to carry when somebody else handed them to you.

The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. David says, "The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue." (2 Samuel 23:2). The Spirit speaks through David, and the word on his tongue is God's. A good messenger knows whose word he's carrying, and David puts it right up front, friends.

The answer is with justice and in the fear of God. The Rock of Israel says the ruler is the one "…who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God…" (2 Samuel 23:3). Two things, and both are about how he rules. Nothing in there about how big the castle is, bakers.

The answer is like morning light at a cloudless dawn. God says that ruler "…is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn…" (2 Samuel 23:4). Picture that first light with not one cloud in the way, friends. That's the picture God chose for a ruler who rules with justice.

The answer is False. God's picture has "…the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth." (2 Samuel 23:4). So the grass is glistening after the rain and it's sprouting. No dry, crunchy grass in this one, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "…He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part." (2 Samuel 23:5). Everlasting means it doesn't run out. David is pretty sure of it, and I'd say with good reason, bakers.

The answer is his full salvation and every desire. David asks, "Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?" (2 Samuel 23:5). He asks it right after talking about the covenant, so I bet he's leaning on God's promise. He sure sounds confident to me, friends.

The answer is thorns raked aside. David says, "But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside…" (2 Samuel 23:6). He adds that "…they can never be gathered by hand." It's a sharp picture, friends, and I think it's meant to be.
The answer is False. David says these thorns "…can never be gathered by hand." (2 Samuel 23:6). Nobody's scooping them up with bare hands. Anybody who's grabbed a thorny branch knows why, bakers.

The answer is iron, friends. The man who touches them "…must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear." (2 Samuel 23:7). That's some serious gear just to handle thorns. It tells you how prickly they are.

The answer is False. David says, "The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie." (2 Samuel 23:7). The verse doesn't mention any trip, just the fire and the place where they lie. And that's how the poem ends, friends.
